title: UstarPay Selects BitGo Bank & Trust for Digital Asset Custody Supporting Its Payment and Card Infrastructure
summary: UstarPay has engaged BitGo Bank & Trust, N.A., an OCC-regulated digital asset trust bank, to safeguard digital assets supporting its payment and card infrastructure.
body_markdown:
## Key Takeaways


-


**UstarPay selects BitGo for regulated custody.** UstarPay has engaged BitGo Bank & Trust, N.A., an OCC-regulated digital asset trust bank, to safeguard digital assets supporting its payment and card infrastructure.


-


**Institutional-grade infrastructure for digital asset payments.** BitGo's custody solutions provide UstarPay with regulated asset safekeeping, security controls and governance infrastructure as it expands its payment capabilities.


-


**A model for fintech and payment platforms.** The relationship demonstrates how regulated digital asset custody can support fintech platforms connecting digital assets with everyday financial transactions.


As digital assets become increasingly integrated into everyday payments, the infrastructure supporting those transactions is becoming just as important as the payment experience itself.


[UstarPay](https://ustarpay.com/?lang=en) , a PayFi platform connecting supported digital assets with card-based spending and transactions, has engaged BitGo Bank & Trust, National Association, an OCC-regulated digital asset trust bank, to provide custody for digital assets supporting its payment and card infrastructure.


Through this relationship, UstarPay gains access to BitGo's regulated custody infrastructure, combining regulated asset safekeeping with established security and governance controls to support its growing digital asset payment ecosystem.


## Bringing Regulated Custody to Digital Asset Payments


Digital asset payment platforms must balance the convenience and accessibility users expect with the security and operational controls required to safeguard customer assets.


For platforms like UstarPay, this means establishing a custody foundation that supports the movement of digital assets across wallets, payment services and card-based spending experiences.


By engaging BitGo Bank & Trust as its custodian, UstarPay can rely on established institutional custody infrastructure rather than building and maintaining its own digital asset safekeeping systems.


The relationship supports UstarPay's ability to:


-


**Safeguard digital assets:** Use regulated custody infrastructure designed to protect assets through institutional security controls.


-


**Strengthen operational governance:** Support asset management and transfer activity through established custody and authorization processes.


-


**Support platform growth:** Build on a custody foundation as UstarPay develops its digital asset payment and card offerings.


For UstarPay, this allows the platform to focus on developing its payment services and user experience while relying on BitGo's custody expertise to safeguard supported digital assets.


## Regulated Custody Built for Institutional Security


BitGo Bank & Trust, N.A. is an[OCC-regulated](https://www.bitgo.com/resources/blog/bitgo-secures-occ-approval/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=apac&utm_campaign=ustarpaypartnership) digital asset trust bank.


Its custody infrastructure is designed to meet the security, governance and operational requirements of institutional clients, including fintech and digital asset platforms, integrating digital assets into financial products and services.


Key capabilities include:


-


**Federal regulatory oversight:** BitGo Bank & Trust is chartered and supervised by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC).


-


**Institutional-grade security:**[Offline cold storage](https://www.bitgo.com/resources/blog/crypto-cold-storage-explained/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=apac&utm_campaign=ustarpaypartnership) , distributed key management and multi-party authorization controls help safeguard digital assets.


-


**Segregated custody:** Client assets are held in[segregated custody arrangements](https://www.bitgo.com/products/qualified-custody/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=apac&utm_campaign=ustarpaypartnership) , separate from the custodian's proprietary assets.


-


**Insurance and independent audits:** BitGo maintains up to[$250 million in custody insurance coverage](https://bitgo.com/resources/blog/qualified-custody-accounts/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=apac&utm_campaign=ustarpaypartnership) , subject to applicable policy terms, and undergoes independent SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type 2 audits.


## What This Means for Fintechs and Payment Platforms


The relationship shows how a payment platform can connect digital assets to everyday spending while a regulated custodian safeguards the assets and operates the security and governance controls.


For fintechs, payment providers and other platforms building digital asset products, BitGo provides regulated custody infrastructure to support their business needs.


[Learn more about BitGo's regulated custody solutions](https://www.bitgo.com/products/qualified-custody/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=apac&utm_campaign=ustarpaypartnership) or[contact our team](https://calendly.com/d/crmk-p2t-k78?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=apac&utm_campaign=ustarpaypartnership) to discuss how BitGo can support your digital asset infrastructure.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Are UstarPay's services available in my jurisdiction?


Availability depends on applicable laws and regulations, user eligibility, supported assets and geographic restrictions. Contact UstarPay to confirm what applies to you.


### What role does BitGo play in UstarPay's infrastructure?


BitGo Bank & Trust, National Association, an OCC-regulated digital asset trust bank and subsidiary of BitGo Holdings, Inc., provides regulated custody for the digital assets supporting UstarPay's payment and card infrastructure.


### Can other payment and fintech platforms use BitGo custody?


Yes. BitGo provides digital asset custody solutions for institutional clients, including fintechs and financial service providers. Availability depends on the applicable entity, jurisdiction and product requirements.
